newsitem.title: GERMANY: German quality coffee roaster aims to raise sales.
newsitem.headline: German quality coffee roaster aims to raise sales.

text.p: German coffee roaster J.J. Darboven aimed to increase volume sales between five and nine percent in 1997, having raised sales by an estimated 10-15 percent this year, chairman Albert Darboven said.
"We're pleased by the expansion in sales and trust in our strategy of maintaining a high quality and serving niche markets," he said in an interview.
The farmily-owned group in 1995 sold 24,000 tonnes of roasted coffee worth 469 million marks.

Darboven would not comment on sales revenue but criticised price fights in the retail sector which he said had undermined roasters' margins despite a consumer tendency towards higher quality products.
Apart from supermarkets, Darboven supplies canteen, airline and hotel coffee vendors, which account for 20-25 percent of all coffee consumption.
The company has a seven percent market share in Germany, where green coffee equivalent consumption this year is expected unchanged at 1995's 564,000 tonnes.
Darboven products cost about 1.00-1.50 marks more than the average roasted coffee which is priced at around 7.00 marks per 500 grams.
Darboven said the company maintained its use of Colombians in its blends at 35-45 percent during tightness in that origin this year, which had resulted in firm differentials.
Other coffee consumers replaced large parts of their usual Colombia intake with Central American and African arabicas as well as Brazils, traders have said.

Darboven said he was hoping a proposed purchase of coffee roaster Eduscho GmbH & Co KG by its competitor Tchibo could help underpin retail prices rather than cause damaging price campaigns between the merged company and market leader KJS.
Family-owned Tchibo/Eduscho and Kraft Jacobs Suchard, part of the Philip Morris group, would battle for market leadership above the 30 percent mark each, if the sale was approved.
But Darboven believed Tchibo's strategy might involve stressing coffee quality and maintaining firm prices.

"Our company will stay out of these developments...I think the consumer will trust and reward a small market segment where he can rely on consistent quality," Darboven said. --Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom +49-40-41903275
